overview.headline: Rebasing a price index to a new reference period

keyPoints.point: Students learn it is sometimes necessary to use index values on a reference base that is not published for contracts and graphs.
keyPoints.quote: It is sometimes necessary to use index values on a reference base that is not published.

keyPoints.point: Students learn the only difference between series is the year set to 100 and the rate of change is exactly the same.
keyPoints.quote: the only difference between series is the year we set to 100, the rate of change is exactly the same.

keyPoints.point: Students learn to find the relative for each data point by dividing it by the previous data point.
keyPoints.quote: First, we must find the relative for each data point in the series by dividing it by the previous data point.

keyPoints.point: Students learn to select any period to set equal to 100 as the new base and chain relatives by multiplying previous index values.
keyPoints.quote: we can select any period to set equal to 100 (the new base) and chain the relatives from that value

keyTerms.gloss: A statistical index that tracks price level and allows comparison of values across reference periods
keyTerms.quote: It is sometimes necessary to use index values on a reference base that is not published.

keyTerms.gloss: The period set equal to 100 that defines index values used for comparison
keyTerms.quote: It is sometimes necessary to use index values on a reference base that is not published.

keyTerms.gloss: The ratio obtained by dividing a current value by the previous data point
keyTerms.quote: First, we must find the relative for each data point in the series by dividing it by the previous data point.

keyTerms.gloss: The change in index values expressed as percent between two periods
keyTerms.quote: The December-December 12-month percent changes of the CPI-U U.S. city average all items series for these two bases

keyTerms.gloss: A published price measure for urban consumers that tracks average change in city items
keyTerms.quote: One alternate base is published for the Consumer Price Index for all urban consumers (CPI-U) in addition to the standard 1982-1984=100 base.
